core_scope: Theorem 1.1 as printed on native 149-151: on a smooth manifold with a complete sub-Riemannian structure (Delta,g) and a fixed x, if for almost every y all minimizing horizontal paths from x to y have Goh-rank at most 1, then the closed set Abn^min(x) has Lebesgue measure zero. Goh-rank of a horizontal path is defined at native 147 as the dimension of the space of abnormal lifts psi in Delta-perp satisfying the Goh condition psi(t) dot [Delta,Delta](gamma(t)) = 0 for all t (native 140-142).
proof_span_note: Theorem 1.1 carries no proof environment of its own. Its complete author proof is printed Section 4, native 932-1706, which closes at native 1705 with 'So, the proof of Theorem 1.1 is complete.' The fifteen numbered results inside that section, 4.1 to 4.15, are the author's own steps of this single proof and appear in complete_author_proof_support_spans, not as separate units. The structure index reports proof_start_line 203 and proof_end_line 209 for Theorem 1.1; that pointer is a nearest-preceding-block default and is not the proof of the theorem. Section 5 opens at native 1707.

items.use: Agrachev and Sarychev: a singular minimizing horizontal path that is not the projection of a normal extremal admits an abnormal lift satisfying the Goh condition.

Agrachev and Lee: absence of Goh-condition abnormal lifts along all minimizing paths from x to y makes the pointed distance Lipschitz near y. This is the quoted result whose hypothesis the current theorem weakens from absence to Goh-rank at most 1.
Cited argument for one implication inside the proof of the characterization proposition PROPcharac.

Agrachev and Sachkov: sufficient condition for local openness of a mapping at second order. The paper says the lemma at native 1131 follows from an extension of it and refers to the appendix for the statement and proof.
The appendix theorem A.1 at native 1811-1829 is presented by the author as a refinement of this book statement, drawing on as04 Chapter 20 and al09 Section 5.
Denjoy-Young-Saks theorem on the four Dini derivatives, used in Remark 2.10.
Chitour, Jean and Trelat: co-rank 1 for nontrivial singular horizontal paths on a dense open set of totally nonholonomic rank m distributions. Supports Corollary 1.4 only.
Lebesgue density point property of measurable sets, quoted in Section 4.
Agrachev: the abnormal minimizing set always has empty interior. Background for the conjecture only.
